# Project name

State the user or developer outcome and the layer this project owns. Name an
important adjacent concern only when clarifying that it belongs elsewhere.

## Project brief

| | |
|---|---|
| User outcome | What becomes possible. |
| Developer focus | The implementation or maintenance problem. |
| Owns | Maintained source, documents, recipes, tests, or patches in this project. |
| Depends on | Upstream and downstream layers required for the outcome. |
| Code lives in | External tree and branch role, without copying a moving tip. |
| Current boundary | Stable link to the public status row or maintained evidence owner. |

## Entry points

List the small set of documents, runbooks, and tests a reader should choose
between first. Save an exhaustive tracked-file inventory for **File index**.

## Technical model

Give the shortest useful model and link the maintained deep explanation. Do
not copy a release ledger, case matrix, or moving source pin here.

## Build or operate

Link the canonical runbook or give one safe first-use command when this audience
needs it.

## Validate

Link the canonical test entry point and state what a pass establishes. Route
exact results and identities to their evidence owner.

## Boundaries and next proof

Name stable limitations. Link the status next-gate row or canonical live plan
for changing work; do not maintain another backlog here.

## Related layers

Link the explicit upstream and downstream project front doors.

## File index

Name every maintained file owned by this README, keeping the curated entry
points above this exhaustive inventory.
